page_title: Sleepr · Bedtime, on autopilot for your Mac.

sources.entry: Sleepr - Sleepr brings back sleep timer on macOS. [![App Store][app-store Icon]](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/sleepr-app/id6465683427?platform=mac)

summary.name: Sleepr
summary.one_liner: Sleepr is a native macOS menu bar app that puts your Mac to sleep on a timer, on a recurring bedtime schedule, or by voice via Siri and Shortcuts.
use_cases: Stop the Mac from running overnight after you fall asleep
Schedule a recurring nightly bedtime for the Mac
Sleep the Mac after a podcast, show, or album ends
Start or stop a sleep countdown by voice with Siri
Get a heads-up before the Mac sleeps so you can extend or cancel
summary.what_it_does: Sleepr lives in the macOS menu bar and runs on-demand timers (presets or an exact clock time, with midnight handled) that trigger a normal system sleep. Recurring schedules let you pick days, a time, and a duration to start timers automatically. A floating HUD-style alert appears a few minutes before the timer ends, including over fullscreen apps, letting you extend or cancel. Four App Intents expose start, set bedtime, check countdown, and stop actions to Siri, Shortcuts, and Focus automations. The page says timers survive app quits and reboots and show a depleting ring, waning moon, or shrinking pie.
notable: Brings back scheduled sleep that macOS removed from System Settings in Ventura
Siri, Shortcuts and Focus integration via four App Intents
Floating alert appears even over fullscreen apps before sleep
No analytics, accounts or server; settings stay on the Mac
caveats: One-time purchase on the Mac App Store; the page does not state the price
